name: resource-loading-review
title: Resource loading review
description: Time-phased resource loading of a P6 project per month or week: per resource the totals, the peak period and the over-allocated periods against what its calendar and max units allow, the periods over the limit and the resources without a limit (read only). Use when the user asks about resource loading, histograms, peaks or over-allocated resources.

args.name: project
args.description: Project ID as shown in P6

args.name: resource
args.description: Resource ID to review alone (empty: every resource)

template:
Resource loading review of project {project} per {period}: for each resource (or resource {resource} alone when it is given) the totals, the peak period and the over-allocated periods, then the periods over the limit and the resources without a limit, with fixed follow-up actions. Nothing is written to the database.

This skill gives you every figure: you copy fields, you never compute them.
- reference/spec.json: the calls, the slots (each a field of one call) and the tables.
- reference/fields.md: for every slot and table column, its field, unit, format and meaning.
- reference/report.md: the report to fill.
- reference/checks.md: stop rules and checks to run before answering.
- reference/example.md: the report filled on a demo project (an example of the format, not of the figures).

Calls, in this order. Each call is one page: the report shows that page and says when there are more,
so do not read further pages.
1. rl = p6_resource_loading(project="{project}", period="{period}", resource="{resource}", limit=200): time-phased load per resource and period against its limit, totals, peaks and counts.
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (resource).

Write the report:
1. Start from reference/report.md. Replace each slot placeholder (a slot name in curly braces) by the field
   named in spec.json slots (call and path), written in the slot's format (reference/fields.md). An argument
   written <name> in these instructions is the placeholder of that name in curly braces in report.md and
   checks.md: the value given (an empty optional argument is left out of the calls).
2. Replace each line [table: name] by that table: one row per item of its list, in the order returned, at
   most its cap, every cell in its column's format, the heads as in spec.json. A table with a totals entry
   ends with its Total row, taken from the totals of its call, never from adding the rows. Only a table
   built from the rows list of its call ends, when that call has more pages (next_offset not null), with
   the line "Showing the first <returned> of <total> <noun>." (returned and total of that call). A table
   built from another list or dict of the call (weeks, paths, roots, causes, counts...) ends with "Only the
   first <cap> <noun> are shown." when that list is longer than the cap, and never with a Showing line. An
   empty list gives the table's empty text; a call that failed or was skipped gives no table.
3. Keep the lines between [if: slot] and [end if] only when the slot is true (true, a number other than 0,
   a text or list that is not empty, an ID - name whose ID is not null), the lines between [if not: slot]
   and [end if] only when it is not; remove the markers.
4. Numbers: take the number as written in the result and round it, halves away from zero, to the decimals
   of its format (-104274.95 in n1 is -104,275.0); whole numbers and counts take a comma between thousands
   (1,227), also in the Showing lines. A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text, and so
   is an ID - name whose ID is null.
5. Never add, subtract, divide, count rows or match rows of two results: a figure that is not a slot or a
   table cell is left out. Ignore the note fields of the tools unless a slot names them.
6. Write the headings and sentences in the user's language; keep values, IDs, names and number formats
   exactly as formatted.
7. Run reference/checks.md before answering. Report a failed cross-check, never hide it; say nothing about
   the checks that pass.

For this skill:
- Labor and nonlabor quantities are hours; material quantities are in the material's own unit (column Unit)
  and are never compared with a limit or added to hours.
- The actions are the fixed sentences of report.md only.

files.text:
# Resource loading review of {project}

Data date {data_date}, last schedule run (F9) {last_f9}. Read only: nothing was written to the database.

[if: stale]
Warning: this project was changed after its last F9. Dates and loading are out of date until it is rescheduled in P6 (F9).
[end if]

[if not: total_rows]
No assignments: {project} has no resource assignment to review (none on the resource given, when one was given). Assign resources in P6, or run this skill without a resource.
[end if]

[if: total_rows]
## Summary

- Resources with assignments: {res_count}, of which material: {material}. Resource periods loaded: {total_rows}.
- Over-allocated resource periods: {over_periods}, on {res_over} resources.
- Labor and nonlabor resources without a limit (no max units or no calendar), never flagged as over-allocated: {no_limit}.

Load = actual (up to the data date) + remaining, spread over the working time of each assignment's calendar. Available = working hours of the resource's calendar x its max units per hour. Labor and nonlabor quantities are hours; material quantities are in the material's own unit and have no limit.

## By resource

[table: resources]

## Over-allocated periods

[table: over]
[end if]

## Actions

Only the actions that apply:

[if: stale]
- Reschedule the project in P6 (F9) before using the loading: it was changed after its last F9.
[end if]
[if: over_periods]
- Over-allocated resource periods: {over_periods}, on {res_over} resources. Level these resources or review their max units and calendars with the planner.
[end if]
[if: no_limit]
- Resources without a limit: {no_limit}. Enter their max units per hour and calendar in P6 to check their loading.
[end if]

# Checks before answering

## Stop rules (write the sentence, then stop)

- A call says the project is not found: "Project <project> was not found: check the Project ID (p6_list_projects)."
- A call says the resource is not found: "Resource <resource> was not found: check the Resource ID (p6_resource_summary)."
- p6_resource_loading says the project has no data date: repeat its message and stop.
- rl.total is 0: write the report with its "No assignments" block only (title, data date, that block, the
  actions), then stop.

## Cross-checks (each group must be equal)

1. rl.data_date = rl.schedule_state.data_date (same data date).

If it differs, the database changed during the call: run it again once. If it still differs, say so and do
not publish the figures.

## Before sending

- Every number, date and count is a slot or a table cell of reference/fields.md, copied from its field
  and written in its format. Nothing was added, subtracted, divided, counted or matched by you.
- The resources table keeps the order returned and stops at 30 rows ("Only the first 30 resources are
  shown." when rl.resources holds more). The over-allocated table lists the rows of the page whose over is
  true, at most 30; when rl.next_offset is not null it ends with "Showing the first <returned> of <total>
  resource periods." and the over-allocated count of the summary (from counts) still covers every period.
- Every resource is written "Resource ID - name".
- An over-allocated periods cell is "no limit" when the resource has no max units or no calendar.
- Material quantities stay in their own unit: they are never added to hours.
- The warning block is kept only when schedule_state.stale is true.
- Headings and sentences are in the user's language; values, IDs, names and number formats exactly as
  formatted.

# Fields of Resource loading review

Generated from reference/spec.json by the catalog build. Each slot of reference/report.md is copied from one field of one call; write it in its format, never compute it.

## Calls

1. rl = p6_resource_loading(project="{project}", period="{period}", resource="{resource}", limit=200): time-phased load per resource and period against its limit, totals, peaks and counts.
Leave out an argument whose value is empty (resource).

## Formats

- text: the value as returned
- int: the whole number, a comma between thousands: 1,227
- date: the first 10 characters: YYYY-MM-DD
- datetime: the first 16 characters: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
- n0: the number as written in the result rounded to a whole number, halves away from zero, a comma between thousands: 12,345
- n1: the same to 1 decimal: 12,345.6 (-104274.95 gives -104,275.0)
- n2: the same to 2 decimals: 12,345.67
- pct1: the same to 1 decimal, then %: 49.7%
- flag: yes for true, no for false
- id_name: the two fields joined: ID - Name (the ID alone when the name is null, the none text when the ID is null)
- list: the items of the list in their order, joined by a comma and a space: in_progress, finishing
- A null value is written as the slot's or column's none text (n/a unless stated).
- [if: slot] is true for true, a number other than 0, a text or list that is not empty.

## Arguments

- {project}: Project ID as shown in P6, as given
- {period}: Loading period: month or week, as given
- {resource}: Resource ID to review alone (empty: every resource), as given

## Units

- qty: resource units: hours for labor and nonlabor, the material's own unit for material
- %: percent
- count: a count

## Slots

| Slot | Field (call.path) | Unit | Format | None | Meaning |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| data_date | rl.data_date |  | date | n/a | data date |
| last_f9 | rl.schedule_state.last_schedule_date |  | datetime | n/a | last F9 in P6 |
| stale | rl.schedule_state.stale |  | flag | n/a | changed by this server after the last F9 |
| total_rows | rl.total | count | int | n/a | resource periods (one row per resource and loaded period) |
| res_count | rl.counts.resources | count | int | n/a | resources with assignments |
| over_periods | rl.counts.over_allocated_periods | count | int | n/a | over-allocated resource periods (labor and nonlabor) |
| res_over | rl.counts.resources_over | count | int | n/a | resources over their limit in at least one period |
| material | rl.counts.material_resources | count | int | n/a | material resources (own unit, no limit) |
| no_limit | rl.counts.no_limit |  | list | none | labor and nonlabor resources without a max units limit or a calendar |

## Table resources

One row per resource, labor and nonlabor first, then material: stored quantities, the peak period and the over-allocated periods (n/a: no limit).

Rows: rl.resources, in the order returned, at most 30 (a dict gives one row per item: its key is _key, a plain value _value).
When the list holds more than 30 items, add the line: Only the first 30 resources are shown.
No rows: write 'No resource is assigned.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Resource | resource + name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Kind | kind |  | text | n/a |  |
| Unit | unit |  | text | n/a |  |
| Budget | budget | qty | n1 | n/a |  |
| Actual | actual | qty | n1 | n/a |  |
| Remaining | remaining | qty | n1 | n/a |  |
| At completion | at_completion | qty | n1 | n/a |  |
| Max units/h | max_units_per_hour |  | n2 | n/a |  |
| Peak period | peak.period |  | text | n/a |  |
| Peak load | peak.load | qty | n1 | n/a |  |
| Available at peak | peak.available | qty | n1 | n/a |  |
| Peak load % | peak.load_pct | % | pct1 | n/a |  |
| Over-allocated periods | over_periods | count | int | no limit |  |

## Table over

The resource periods of the page whose load (actual + remaining) is above what the resource can give.

Rows: rl.rows, in the order returned, at most 30, only the rows whose over is true.
When rl.next_offset is not null, add the line: Showing the first <returned> of <total> resource periods. (returned and total of rl).
No rows: write 'No period is over-allocated on this page.' instead of the table (nothing when the call failed).

| Column | Field (row path) | Unit | Format | None | In totals row |
|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Resource | resource + name |  | id_name | n/a |  |
| Period | period |  | text | n/a |  |
| Load | load | qty | n1 | n/a |  |
| Available | available | qty | n1 | n/a |  |
| Load % | load_pct | % | pct1 | n/a |  |
| Over by | over_by | qty | n1 | n/a |  |

## Cross-checks (equal values)

- same data date: rl.data_date = rl.schedule_state.data_date
